page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is shared, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with single-thread-per-core execution. The system features 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for multi-threaded decompression and stress-ng multi-core tests. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is also strong, though write bandwidth and small-block cached read bandwidth remain in the average tier. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference text generation using a small model achieves top-tier speeds, while prompt processing falls into the average range.

The server presents a specific trade-off between high-capacity memory and shared CPU allocation. While the 192.0 GB RAM capacity and dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU provide a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive and parallel processing tasks, the shared CPU allocation may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU compute loads. Lacking local storage, the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage solutions. This configuration is well-suited for machine learning inference, data science workloads, GPU-accelerated rendering, and memory-heavy analytical databases.
